3|# Handoff 01 - claude: framing panel - reviewers that propose remedies, not only verdicts
4|
5|Date: 2026-10-22. Base commit: C3 `23d49ad` (main; 0.2.3 under acceptance). C3 is a bridge that lets a
6|coordinating agent (Claude Code) consult a roster of reviewer models from different labs through their CLIs; every
7|consultation is recorded as files under `.collab/<task>/` (brief, verbatim reply, `sessions.json` ledger,
8|`findings.json` store); a panel runs several reviewers on one brief; a routed panel seats reviewers by track record
9|(`README.md` "Reviewer roster and panel"; `docs/DESIGN.md` for the invariants: files are the record, reviewers are
10|read-only, the coordinator decides).
11|
12|## The situation that prompted this panel
13|
14|The release 0.2.3 is in an acceptance loop with one standing reviewer (openai :: gpt-6-astra, "Astra"):
15|
16|- pass 1 (`.collab/parity-0.6.1-2026-10-08/handoffs/89-codex-codex-0.2.3-acceptance-1.reply.json`): HOLD, 3
17|  blockers + 5 more findings in the new `c3 work` feature (a roster model run as a coding worker);
18|- the coordinator briefed a Claude Code worker, which fixed all eight (`docs/port/wave10a-work-acceptance.md`);
19|- pass 2 (`handoffs/91-codex-codex-0.2.3-acceptance-2.reply.json`): HOLD again - 4 findings (F91-1..F91-4), two of
20|  them "the fix closed the simple case, this is the remaining case" of the pass-1 blockers.
21|
22|Each finding carries `claim`, `trigger`, `verification` and a short `remedy` (one sentence: "validate the permitted
23|state, exhaustion, owner and expected attempt generation under the admission lock"). The remedy is a direction, not
24|a design: the worker that implements it makes the design choices alone, and the next pass finds the case it missed.
25|Cost today: about 280 s and 9-16 % of Astra's 5-hour window per pass; a worker wave of 40-60 minutes between passes.
26|
27|## The operator's proposal (to be challenged)
28|
29|When a reviewer raises a blocker, the OTHER roster members - preferably models from other labs than the finder -
30|propose concrete remedies (design + where in the code + the test that proves it); the coordinator picks one (or
31|merges), the worker implements it, and the finding is verified. Rationale: the model that found the problem should
32|not be the one that designs the fix (it would confirm its own frame), independent solvers see the cases the finder
33|listed and the ones it did not, and vendor diversity turns one reviewer's taste into a decision between
34|alternatives. The roles would be: finder (raises, states acceptance criteria), solvers (propose), coordinator
35|(chooses), verifier (the finder, or a third member?).
36|
37|## What exists in the bridge that this would build on
38|
39|- The reply schema already has `findings[].remedy` and `prior_findings[]` with per-id status
40|  (`crates/c3/src/consult/` ingests it; `c3 findings` lists, sets status `proposed|implemented|verified|rejected`).
41|- Panels with roles: `--role <one for all>` / `--roles <by score rank>` (`crates/c3/src/panel/roles.rs`, Kuhn
42|  matching on willingness) - a seat can be told "you are a solver for F91-1".
43|- Routing by track record: `panel.routing`, ratings `useful yes|partly|no` per consultation keyed by
44|  `consult_id`, the router scores reviewer x purpose x topic (`crates/c3/src/router/`).
45|- Packs: `c3 pack` builds a token-budgeted, sanitised context of named files for a model that cannot read the
46|  repository (`crates/c3/src/pack/`); the `http` engine consults OpenRouter models with a pack.
47|- Workers: `c3 work` runs a roster model as a coding worker that edits the tree (`docs/work-mode.md`).
48|
49|## The coordinator's sketch
50|
51|A new purpose `remedy` (preset effort high): `c3 consult --remedy F91-1[,F91-2] --panel-size 3 --exclude-vendor
52|<finder's lab>`; the brief is generated from the finding record (claim, trigger, verification, remedy, locations)
53|plus a pack of the located code and the tests that exist; every member answers with `proposals[]` {approach, code
54|locations, patch sketch, test, risks, confidence}; the proposals are stored under the finding id in `findings.json`
55|(`findings[].proposals[]` with the proposer's identity); the coordinator marks one `adopted` and the rest
56|`rejected` with a reason; the finder verifies on the next pass; the adoption marks feed the router as a second
57|score dimension ("solver" next to "finder"), so a member can be routed as a good solver even if it is a mediocre
58|finder. Automatic trigger: on a HOLD with blockers, the coordinator is offered the exact `--remedy` line (it is not
59|run automatically - the window cost is the coordinator's to spend).
60|
61|## Questions
62|
63|- **Q1.** Is the separation finder / solver / verifier sound, and who should verify - the finder (it knows the
64|  trigger), a third member, or a test the solver must ship? Name the failure modes: a solver that does not know
65|  the codebase, a finder that rejects every foreign fix, the cost of three consultations per blocker.
66|- **Q2.** The design: what is the minimal `proposals[]` record and workflow (purpose, roles, exclusion of the
67|  finder's vendor, pack contents, how the coordinator records the choice) that fits the existing files-are-the-
68|  record ledger? What must NOT be automated?
69|- **Q3.** Live demonstration. Pick at least two of F91-1, F91-2, F91-3, F91-4 (read the reply.json of handoff 91;
70|  the code is `crates/c3/src/work/mod.rs` - `claim_for_spawn`, `resume_once`, `refresh_artifacts`, `classify_attempt`;
71|  `crates/c3/src/work/record.rs` - `read_record`, `run_dirs`, `live_run`, `admission_lock`;
72|  `crates/c3/src/work/engines.rs` - `terminal_outcome`) and propose a concrete remedy for each: the design, the
73|  exact function(s) to change, the invariant it establishes, and the test (name + what it drives) that proves it.
74|  If you ARE the finder (openai :: gpt-6-astra), do not propose solutions: state per finding the acceptance criteria
75|  - the evidence that closes it - so the solvers' proposals can be judged against them.
76|- **Q4.** Scoring: how should an adopted proposal and a verified fix be credited (to the solver, to the finder, to
77|  both), so the router learns "good solver" without the finder gaming it by raising easy blockers?
78|
79|Answer by number. Put each recommendation and each Q3 proposal as a finding (`claim` = the recommendation or the
80|proposed remedy, `trigger` = the case it addresses, `verification` = the test or evidence, `remedy` = the design in
81|two to five sentences). Keep it under 700 words. Reading budget: at most 6 tool calls; never print a whole file.
